bio_en: Hovhannes Devejian, pen-name Armen Sevan, was born in 1892 in Mashkert near Arabkir, studied in Aleppo and at the Berberian school in Scutari (1911), and followed law courses at the University of Constantinople. Conscripted in 1914, he escaped at great risk to Bulgaria. In 1920 he was in Yerevan, took part in the ARF's 9th General Congress and served as secretary of the Council of Ministers of independent Armenia, and he was involved in the February 1921 uprising. After the Red Army occupied Romania he was arrested with many Dashnaks and sentenced in 1947 to eight years' imprisonment; a poet and educator, he died on 3 May 1976.
